name: App builder — iteration
description: The follow-up loop to “App builder — idea to launch”: keep developing the app after the initial cycle, staffed like a company. The product-manager turns a change request into iteration requirements (reading the previous cycle's reports for context if they exist) → an ENGINEERING HUDDLE: the backend-engineer assesses the change first, the frontend-engineer responds seeing that take (both read the real code, read-only) → the CTO chairs the huddle into the minimal change-set plan, declaring the owning AREA (backend / frontend / fullstack) as its last line → YOUR sign-off → a switch routes the work to the right engineer: backend-engineer, frontend-engineer, or both in sequence for fullstack — all on the delegation idle timeout → full suite with the on-call engineer fixing-and-retesting until green → independent code review → an iteration report proposing the next three iterations. Run it manually per request — or add a chat-keyword trigger (e.g. “iterate on the app”) or a chain trigger to keep the loop firing itself.

input.label: What to build or fix next
input.placeholder: e.g. add weekly streak stats to the dashboard · fix the login redirect loop

nodes.text:
If dev/app-report.md or dev/iteration-report.md exist in the workspace, read them for context (read_file) — they describe the app and its known weaknesses. Then turn this change request into iteration requirements: what changes, what must NOT change (regressions to guard), and 2-5 testable acceptance criteria.

Request: {{input}}

Write the iteration report as Markdown: the request ({{input}}), what changed and why ({{node.3}}), final test status ({{node.10}}), review findings ({{node.13}}) — and finish by proposing the three most valuable NEXT iterations.
